title: Projective morphisms with finite fibres are finite
statement: Let $f:D\to T$ be a projective morphism [def-pc-projective-morphism] with Noetherian target (that is, $T$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). If every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has only finitely many points, then $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $f$ is proper. Since $T$ is Noetherian, it is locally Noetherian by its definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus the properness and base hypotheses of [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] hold; it remains to verify finite ordinary fibres.

Fix any point $t\in T$ and put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $\bar k=\overline{k}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with the commutative $k$-algebra $k$: the map $k\to k\otimes_k\bar k$ is faithfully flat. Under the elementary ring isomorphism $k\otimes_k\bar k\simeq\bar k$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, this is the field inclusion $k\to\bar k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] makes $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ surjective. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre], $D_{\bar t}=D_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to the preceding surjective spectrum map and $D_t\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the projection $D_{\bar t}\to D_t$ is surjective. The source has finitely many points by hypothesis, so its image, all of $D_t$, is finite. Finally [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the underlying space of $D_t$ with $f^{-1}(t)$. Therefore every ordinary set-theoretic fibre is finite, including the empty case.

proof.text: For every $t\in T$, step 2 proves that $f^{-1}(t)$ is finite. Step 1 proves properness, and the target is locally Noetherian. Apply implication (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1) of [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] with $X=D$ and $S=T$ to conclude that $f$ is finite.
